sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and data shapes
sections.what: Brings in the network library and the shapes of the data the app sends and receives, such as inputs, outputs, sessions and model responses.
sections.why: The shapes let the editor check that data is used with the fields it is expected to have.
sections.watch_out: If a shared type is renamed in the types file, this file will stop compiling.

sections.name: APIClient (part 1)
sections.title: Client setup and session basics
sections.what: Creates the client with the /api address, JSON headers, a 60-second limit, and an error logger. Also includes simple calls to check the server is alive, create a session, read one session, and list sessions.
sections.why: Likely reason: setting the address and limit once means every request shares the same behaviour.
sections.watch_out: The 60-second limit applies to every request, so a calculation that runs longer fails on this side even if the server keeps working.

sections.name: APIClient: deleteSession
sections.title: Session removal and calculation calls
sections.what: Covers deleting a session, running a full calculation, running a quick calculation that returns cost numbers only, updating input values in a session, and fetching the breakdown for one component.
sections.why: The full calculation includes lecture and web research unless the caller turns them off, which is why it takes longer.
sections.watch_out: Full calculations with research are the requests most likely to hit the 60-second limit.

sections.name: APIClient: getLectureStep
sections.title: Lecture, export, and defaults calls
sections.what: Fetches one numbered lecture step for a session, exports the session to an Excel file, and fetches the default inputs.
sections.why: Likely reason: the lecture is split into numbered steps so each can be fetched on its own, and the Excel file is binary so it is handled as a Blob rather than as text.
sections.watch_out: The step number must match a step the backend actually created, or the request will fail.

sections.name: apiClient
sections.title: Shared client and named exports
sections.what: Creates one shared client object, then copies its methods out as named exports so other files can import them one by one.
sections.why: Likely reason: a convenience so callers can import a single function without the whole object.
sections.watch_out: Copied-out methods lose the link to the connection object they rely on, so calling them this way can fail; check before using these names.

summary: The single place where the web app talks to its Python backend over the network, with one method for each backend action.
purpose: Hides web addresses and request details so the rest of the app can simply call a method such as calculate or getDefaults.
why: Likely reason: keeping all network calls in one file makes them easy to find and change. The 60-second wait is set because calculations can be slow.
how: Creates one connection object pointed at the /api address, with JSON headers and a 60-second time limit. Each method sends one request (read, create, update, delete, calculate, or export) and returns the data from the response. A shared logger prints any failed request to the console, then passes the error on to the caller.
inputs: Method arguments such as the cost model inputs, session IDs, a component name, a lecture step number, and calculation options that switch lecture and web research on or off.
outputs: Data returned by the backend: session information, cost results, lecture steps, validation details, default inputs, or an Excel file held in memory as a Blob.
risks: Errors are passed back to the caller, so any caller that does not handle them will fail silently. The 60-second limit may cut off a slow calculation. The convenience exports at the bottom take methods off the connection object, which can break them if callers use them that way.
debug: Open the browser developer console: each failed request is logged with the backend's error message. Confirm the backend is running and that the route names match the server. An error saying a property of undefined cannot be read points to the detached methods at the bottom of the file.
